name: rs485
title: RS-485 at 3.3 V: MAX3485 with switchable termination, idle bias and DE pull-down
about: Half-duplex RS-485 transceiver for a 3.3 V MCU: MAX3485 with DE and RE# joined and pulled down, so the driver stays off and the receiver on while the firmware starts; 120 Ω termination behind a DIP switch, on at the two nodes at the cable ends; idle (failsafe) bias of 270 Ω from A to 3.3 V and from B to ground, so an idle terminated bus reads 1, not noise; pull-ups on RO and DI keep the UART lines at idle while they are released (maker-coverage BL-10, CK-17).

ports.a: bus line A (non-inverting) – to the connector
ports.b: bus line B (inverting) – to the connector
ports.ro: receiver output – to the MCU's UART RX
ports.di: driver input – from the MCU's UART TX
ports.de: direction: DE and RE# joined – high transmits, low receives; low until the firmware drives it
ports.gnd: ground – also the ground wire that runs with the pair

components.label: {as}: DE/RE# pull-down 10 k
components.notes: Driver off, receiver on from power-up until the firmware drives the pin: the MAX3485 has no internal pull on DE.

components.label: {as}: RO pull-up 10 k
components.notes: RO is high impedance while RE# is high (transmitting): RX stays at idle instead of floating.

components.label: {as}: DI pull-up 10 k
components.notes: TX floats until the firmware sets up the UART; held at idle, a driver enabled early sends no start bit.

components.label: {as}: termination on/off
components.notes: On at the two nodes at the ends of the cable, off at every node in between.

nets.name: a
nets.notes: 0–5.5 V: a 5 V transceiver may drive the same bus; RS-485's common-mode range (−7 … +12 V) is not declared.

nets.name: term
nets.notes: Between the termination resistor and its switch.

notes: Idle bias 270 Ω: TI SLLA272D, equation 2, RB = VBUS_min / (VAB × (1/375 Ω + 4/Z0)), gives 333 Ω for VBUS_min 3.0 V (the MAX3485's lowest VCC), VAB 0.25 V (200 mV receiver threshold + 50 mV noise, as TI's example) and Z0 120 Ω. The exact divider with both terminations (60 Ω) and 32 unit loads (375 Ω) holds only 218 mV with 330 Ω; 270 Ω holds 262 mV – the design choice here. The idle bus then draws about 5.5 mA from 3.3 V.

One bias pair per bus: the bias adds 540 Ω across the pair, with both terminations 54 Ω – the load at which the MAX3485 guarantees VOD ≥ 1.5 V (data sheet, DC characteristics). On the other nodes of the bus leave R4 and R5 out (remove them from the graph).

Termination: SW1 on at the two nodes at the cable ends, off elsewhere (SLLA272D section 6: 120 Ω, one at each cable end; MAX3485 Figure 21). SW1 is rated 25 mA at 24 V DC (switching life): a lone driver with 2.5–3 V across 120 Ω comes close to it. Where the node is always at an end, a fixed 120 Ω (no switch) is the simpler choice.

edakit counts a termination only as a resistor directly across A–B or split; the 120 Ω behind SW1 is not seen, so REQ.missing/termination reports the bus unterminated – accept it on the A net with the reason ("SW1 switches 120 Ω at this end"). REQ.value/failsafe needs a termination across the pair to compute the idle voltage; without one it assumes the full supply.
DE and RE# joined: the node cannot hear its own transmission; for that, give RE# its own pin (and a pull-down) instead of the shared net.

Bus pins: the MAX3485 limits a shorted driver to ±250 mA and shuts down thermally (C18148 hints) – no series resistors on A/B. Where the bus connector is marked off_board, REQ.missing/leave asks for them anyway: the C18148 entry has no short_proof on A and B. For long or outdoor cables a TVS across A/B to ground (SM712 class) is worth a look; it is not in the block.

sim.json: the DI net under the MCU's outputs (idle high), the RO net under its inputs; a load with "dip_closed": {"SW<n>": [1]} simulates the termination switched on. The MAX3485 has no behaviour model: its supply and driver currents are not simulated.

t_term.about: UART idle, termination switched on (SW2 is the block's SW1 in the example)
